title: Explainable Outlier Detection for Interval-valued Data
Explainable Outlier Detection for Interval-valued Data
summary: Outlier detection for interval-valued data has lacked an explanation layer. The paper derives closed-form Shapley values and a Shapley interaction index for the squared robust Interval-Mahalanobis distance under the IMCD estimator, decomposing outlyingness into centers, ranges, and cross-terms. On the Cars and Spotify datasets it illustrates variable-level explanations and flags outliers consistent with domain knowledge.

text: Cloning into 'repo'...

why: The AIDA repository is a complete, self-contained R package: it ships the intCars.rda data, the IMCD estimator (R/IMCD.r), farness transform (R/farness.r), outlier flagging (R/int_outliers.r), and two vignettes (IMCD_examples.Rmd, Shapley_examples.Rmd) plus executed scripts in inst/doc/ that perform exactly the Cars analysis behind C1-C6 (reweighted IMCD with ~75% subset, 0.9 farness cutoff, Shapley barplot of the six largest distances). No weights, no downloads and no dead frameworks: the only needs are an R runtime and CRAN dependencies.
est_runtime: ~20-30 min: ~10-15 min to install R (if absent) and compile/install AIDA + CRAN deps, ~1-2 min to run the Cars IMCD + farness + Shapley vignette chunk
blockers: This is an R package, not Python: requires installing R plus CRAN dependencies (MAINT.Data, rrcov/robustbase, ggplot2, etc.), which is the bulk of the setup time
MAINT.Data is pinned at version 2.8.0 in the paper; newer CRAN versions may change the Cars import path slightly
IMCD subset selection is stochastic: reaching exactly the five named flags may require fixing the seed / repeating the random subset draw
Nothing renders offline: vignette figures need ggplot2 and the package built/installed (R CMD INSTALL) before the .Rmd will knit

approach: The AIDA repository is an R package, but the sandbox can only execute Python/pip/git, so the plan uses the shipped AIDA sources and vignettes as the executable specification and ports only the tiny Cars pipeline to Python. We read data/intCars.rda with pyreadr/rdata, extract the interval bounds and car labels, then port the reweighted IMCD, farness transform, squared Interval-Mahalanobis distance, and closed-form Shapley/interaction formulas line-by-line from R/IMCD.r, R/farness.r, R/int_distances.r, and R/Shapley.r. The primary target is C1: reproduce the five Figure 1 outlier labels with h=20, farness cutoff 0.9, and strict score>0.9 flagging. The same fit is reused for the Figure 2a top-six and Figure 3 Shapley diagnostics. C2-C6 are recorded in results/metrics.json as intermediate checks rather than separate experiments.
steps: Use Python to ensure third_party/AIDA exists; if not, run git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/catarinaploureiro/AIDA.git third_party/AIDA. Do not modify author files.
Install Python dependencies needed for parsing RData: pip install pyreadr rdata; keep preinstalled numpy, scipy, pandas, matplotlib.

Inspect third_party/AIDA/data/intCars.rda from Python. First try pyreadr; if the intData S4 object is not directly convertible, use rdata to recursively dump object classes and attributes and locate slots LowerBounds, UpperBounds, Centers, Ranges, and Class/labels. Use man/ and R/intData_class.r to identify slot names.

Build the Cars matrix as n=27, p=4 lower/upper arrays with car-model labels. Confirm the four variables are lnPrice, Engine Capacity, Top Speed, and Acceleration; if Price is not already logged, apply natural log to both Price bounds and rename to lnPrice. Drop only the class variable from distance computations.
Compute interval centers c=(a+b)/2 and ranges r=b-a for the four variables. Assert finite values, positive ranges, and no accidental extra variables.
Port the symbolic covariance construction from R/int_cov.r using the Uniform[-1,1] latent moments; verify the 4x4 covariance matrix is symmetric positive definite on the full data.

Implement IMCD in src/imcd.py: for each random start draw h=20 observations, compute symbolic covariance determinant, perform concentration C-steps retaining the h smallest robust distances, and keep the subset with the smallest determinant. Use five seed blocks of 2000 starts and select the best determinant; verify determinant stability across blocks.

Reweight the best IMCD fit: compute farness scores for all 27 observations using the current center/covariance, retain observations with score <= 0.9, recompute the robust barycenter and covariance, and iterate until the retained set is stable. Record the initial h subset size and final reweighted inlier count.

Port the squared robust Interval-Mahalanobis distance from R/int_distances.r and compute distances and farness scores for all 27 Cars observations. Assert all distances and scores are finite and farness scores lie in [0,1].

Flag observations with farness score strictly greater than 0.9. Record the flagged labels in descending squared-distance order. Compare the count to 5 and the labels to MercedesClasseS, Ferrari, Porsche, MercedesSL, and HondaNSK.

Compute Shapley values for all observations using the closed-form expression ported from R/Shapley.r. For Cars set Psi=0 and cross center-range terms to zero per the symmetric uniform assumption. Check that sum_j phi_j equals the squared distance to numerical tolerance 1e-8.
Select the six observations with the largest squared distances, as in Figure 2a, regardless of outlier flag. Confirm the set contains the five expected outliers and Bmwserie7.
Compute the Shapley interaction matrix from Equations (10)-(12), setting diagonal terms so each row sums to that observation's Shapley value. Produce the Ferrari interaction tile data for Figure 3b.

Generate results/figures/cars_farness_outliers.png, cars_shapley_top6.png, cars_center_range_decomp.png, and ferrari_interaction_tile.png. Plot expected versus computed labels where useful for debugging.

Write results/metrics.json with a claim-level section for C1-C6 plus diagnostic arrays: car labels, distances, farness scores, flagged labels, top-six labels/order, h and h-percent, final reweighted count, Shapley efficiency errors, and maximum absolute cross center-range term.
Run python reproduce.py for the full result and verify metrics.json contains C1 count/labels and all intermediate checks. Keep the full run deterministic with the configured seed.
smoke_test: Run `python reproduce.py --smoke`: load intCars and assert shape 27x4, compute centers/ranges, fit IMCD with h=20 and 50 random starts for one seed block, compute distances and farness scores, and run Shapley values for the first observation. Assert finite outputs, covariance determinant >0, and Shapley efficiency error <1e-8. Write results/smoke.json and exit without making full figures. Target runtime <90 seconds.
intermediate_checks: Dataset check: intCars has exactly 27 rows, 4 interval variables, and labels including the five expected car names; class labels are present but excluded from distances.
Preprocessing check: lnPrice lower/upper bounds are on log scale; EngCap, Top Speed, Acceleration are untouched; no extra standardization is applied.
Geometry check: all ranges positive; centers/ranges finite; symbolic covariance symmetric positive definite; condition number below 1e12.
Subset check: h=20, h/n=74.07%, reported as approximately 75%; final reweighted inlier count at score<=0.9 is recorded separately.
IMCD stability check: best covariance determinant agrees across five independent seed blocks to relative tolerance 1e-6; if not, increase starts before proceeding.
Distance sanity check: a classical non-robust interval Mahalanobis baseline should rank the same suspected outliers near the top; large disagreement signals an IMCD/porting bug.
Farness check: all scores in [0,1], values around the 0.9 cutoff are printed with labels so a borderline flag is visible.
C1 check: flagged count must be 5 for exact label match, and within 2 observations for the tolerance-based claim.
C3/C10 check: top six by descending squared distance must include the five expected outliers plus Bmwserie7, with Bmwserie7 present even if not flagged.
Shapley efficiency check: for every observation, |sum(phi)-distance| <= 1e-8.
C6 check: maximum absolute cross centers-ranges Shapley contribution is <= 1e-10 for all Cars observations.
Interaction check: for Ferrari, row sums of the interaction matrix equal the Shapley values to tolerance 1e-8.
budget_plan: Total ~25 minutes. Setup 6-8 min: git clone and pip install pyreadr/rdata plus data introspection. Smoke 1-2 min: 50-start IMCD and one-observation Shapley check. Full fit 6-8 min: five seed blocks of 2000 starts on 27x20 subsets, reweighting, Shapley values and interactions. Figures/metrics 2-3 min. Reserve 4-5 min for debugging S4 extraction or a borderline farness flag; if IMCD starts are slow, reduce to 1000 starts per block only after confirming determinant stability.

    1| #' Farness Estimation
    2| #' 
    3| #' Estimate farness from a distance vector in order to identify outlier observations.
    4| #' 
    5| #' @param dist Vector of distances of each observation.
    6| #' @param cutoff_value Optional cutoff value between 0 and 1 to flag outliers. If provided, the function returns both the farness probabilities and the cutoff distance value in the original distance scale.
    7| #' @return  Either a vector of farness probabilities for each observation (if \code{cutoff_value} is not provided) or a list containing (if \code{cutoff_value} is provided):
    8| #' \item{\code{farness_probs}}{A vector of farness probabilities for each observation. Values between 0 and 1.}
    9| #' \item{\code{cutoff_value}}{The cutoff distance value in the original distance scale corresponding to the specified \code{cutoff_value} probability.}
   10| #' @references J. Raymaekers and P.J. Rousseeuw (2021). Transforming variables to central normality. Machine Learning. \doi{10.1007/s10994-021-05960-5}
   11| #' @references Based on the \code{cellWise} package: Raymaekers J, Rousseeuw P (2023). _cellWise: Analyzing Data with Cellwise Outliers_. R package version 2.5.3, \url{https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=cellWise}.
   12| #' @export
   13| #' @examples
   14| #' data(creditcard)
   15| #' credit_card_int <- creditcard$intData
   16| #' 
   17| #' # Compute squared Interval-Mahalanobis distance
   18| #' credit_card_dist <- IMah_dist(credit_card_int)
   19| #' 
   20| #' credit_card_farness <- farness(credit_card_dist, cutoff_value = 0.9)
   21| farness <- function(dist, cutoff_value=NULL) {
   22|     indnz <- which(dist > 1e-10)
   23|     farnz <- dist[indnz]
   24| 
   25|     # scale the distances
   26|     farloc <- median(farnz, na.rm = TRUE)
   27|     farsca <- mad(farnz, na.rm = TRUE)
   28|     if (farsca < 1e-10) {farsca <- sd(farnz, na.rm = TRUE)}
   29|     sfar <- scale(farnz, center = farloc, scale = farsca)
   30| 
   31|     # apply Yeo-Johnson transformation
   32|     YJout  <- cellWise::transfo(X = sfar, type = "YJ", robust = TRUE, standardize = FALSE, checkPars = list(silent = TRUE))
   33|     xt <- YJout$Y
   34| 
   35|     # scale the transformed distances
   36|     tfarloc <- median(xt, na.rm = TRUE)
   37|     tfarsca <- mad(xt, na.rm = TRUE)
   38|     zt <- scale(xt, tfarloc, tfarsca)
   39|     
   40|     # obtain final probabilities
   41|     probs <- rep(0, length(dist))
   42|     probs[indnz] <- pnorm(zt)
   43|     
   44|     names(probs) <- names(dist)
   45| 
   46|     # cutoff value
   47|     if (!is.null(cutoff_value)) {
   48|         if (cutoff_value>1||cutoff_value<0) stop("cutoff_value must be between 0 and 1")
   49|         cutoff_value <- qnorm(cutoff_value)
   50|         cutoff_value <- cutoff_value * tfarsca + tfarloc
   51|         cutoff_value <- cellWise::transfo_transformback(Ynew = cutoff_value, transfo.out = YJout)
   52|         cutof

    1| #' Outlier Detection for Interval-Valued Data Based on Robust Distances
    2| #'
    3| #' Identifies potential outliers in interval-valued data using robust distance-based methods with customizable cutoff criteria.
    4| #'
    5| #' This function classifies observations as outliers based on robust distances and user-defined cutoff methods. It supports various approaches, including Chi-Squared quantiles, adjusted boxplots, F distribution quantiles, and farness probabilities.
    6| #'
    7| #' @param robust_dist A numeric vector containing the robust distances for each observation.
    8| #' @param cutoff_lvl A numeric value specifying the level of the cutoff to be used. 
    9| #' \itemize{
   10| #'      \item If \code{cutoff="chi-squared"}, \code{cutoff_lvl} is the quantile of the Chi-squared distribution (default is 0.975).
   11| #'      \item If \code{cutoff="adjbox"}, \code{cutoff_lvl} is the coefficient for the adjusted boxplot (default is 1.5).
   12| #'      \item If \code{cutoff="F-dist"}, \code{cutoff_lvl} is the quantile of the F-distribution (default is 0.975).
   13| #'      \item If \code{cutoff="farness"}, \code{cutoff_lvl} represents the threshold for farness, with a default of 0.99.
   14| #'      \item If \code{cutoff="raw"}, \code{cutoff_lvl} is ignored.
   15| #' }
   16| #' If no value is provided, the function uses the default values associated with each cutoff method.
   17| #' @param cutoff A character string specifying the method for setting the outlier cutoff threshold. Options include:
   18| #'   \itemize{
   19| #'      \item \code{"chi-squared"}: Outliers are identified based on a specified Chi-Squared quantile.
   20| #'      \item \code{"adjbox"}: Uses adjusted boxplot statistics (from \code{robustbase}) to classify outliers.
   21| #'      \item \code{"F-dist"}: Applies a cutoff derived from the F and Beta distributions for robust outlier detection.
   22| #'      \item \code{"farness"}: Identifies outliers based on a "farness" threshold, determined by the robust distance distribution.
   23| #'   }
   24| #'   Default is \code{"farness"}.

  265| safe_solve_cov <- function(cov, verbose = TRUE) {
  266|

  270|     }

farness <- function(dist, cutoff_value=NULL) {
    indnz <- which(dist > 1e-10)
    farnz <- dist[indnz]

    # scale the distances
    farloc <- median(farnz, na.rm = TRUE)
    farsca <- mad(farnz, na.rm = TRUE)
    if (farsca < 1e-10) {farsca <- sd(farnz, na.rm = TRUE)}
    sfar <- scale(farnz, center = farloc, scale = farsca)

    # apply Yeo-Johnson transformation
    YJout  <- cellWise::transfo(X = sfar, type = "YJ", robust = TRUE, standardize = FALSE, checkPars = list(silent = TRUE))
    xt <- YJout$Y

    # scale the transformed distances
    tfarloc <- median(xt, na.rm = TRUE)
    tfarsca <- mad(xt, na.rm = TRUE)
    zt <- scale(xt, tfarloc, tfarsca)
    
    # obtain final probabilities
    probs <- rep(0, length(dist))
    probs[indnz] <- pnorm(zt)
    
    names(probs) <- names(dist)

    # cutoff value
    if (!is.null(cutoff_value)) {
        if (cutoff_value>1||cutoff_value<0) stop("cutoff_value must be between 0 and 1")
        cutoff_value <- qnorm(cutoff_value)
        cutoff_value <- cutoff_value * tfarsca + tfarloc
        cutoff_value <- cellWise::transfo_transformback(Ynew = cutoff_value, transfo.out = YJout)
        cutoff_value <- cutoff_value * farsca + farloc

        return(list(farness_probs = probs, cutoff_value = cutoff_value[[1]]))
    } else {
        return(farness_probs = probs)
    }
}

"""Load the interval-valued Cars data from the AIDA package (data/intCars.rda).

The .rda file holds an S4 ``intData`` object (plus the original microdata).  We
read it with the pure-python ``rdata`` parser, pull out the slot values and cache
the 27x4 lower/upper bound matrices as a small .npz so later runs never re-parse
the R serialization.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
import subprocess
import sys

import numpy as np

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
ROOT = os.path.dirname(HERE)
RDA_PATH = os.path.join(ROOT, "repo", "data", "intCars.rda")


def _ensure_rdata():
    try:
        import rdata  # noqa: F401
    except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - environment bootstrap
        subprocess.check_call([sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "install", "rdata"])
        import rdata  # noqa: F401
    return rdata


def cache_dir() -> str:
    d = os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE") or os.path.join(ROOT, "cache")
    os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
    return d


def _npz_path() -> str:
    return os.path.join(cache_dir(), "intCars_interval.npz")


def _parse_rda():
    rdata = _ensure_rdata()
    parsed = rdata.parser.parse_file(RDA_PATH)
    conv = rdata.conversion.convert(parsed.object)
    int_data = conv["intCars"]["intData"]  # S4 -> SimpleNamespace of slots

    lower = np.asarray(int_data.LowerBounds, dtype=float)
    upper = np.asarray(int_data.UpperBounds, dtype=float)
    centers = np.asarray(int_data.Centers, dtype=float)
    ranges = np.asarray(int_data.Ranges, dtype=float)
    varnames = [str(v) for v in np.asarray(int_data.VarNames).ravel()]
    obsnames = [str(v) for v in np.asarray(int_data.ObsNames).ravel()]

    latent_case = str(np.asarray(int_data.LatentCase).ravel()[0])
    latent_param = float(np.asarray(int_data.LatentParam, dtype=float).ravel()[0])
    n_micro = int(np.asarray(int_data.NbMicroUnits, dtype=float).ravel()[0])

    return dict(
        lower=lower,
        upper=upper,
        centers=centers,
        ranges=ranges,
        varnames=np.array(varnames, dtype=object),
        obsnames=np.array(obsnames, dtype=object),
        latent_case=latent_case,
        latent_param=latent_param,
        n_micro=n_micro,
    )


def load_cars(force: bool = False) -> dict:
    """Return dict with lower/upper/centers/ranges (n x p) and labels."""
    path = _npz_path()
    if os.path.exists(path) and not force:
        z = np.load(path, allow_pickle=True)
        return dict(
            lower=z["lower"],
            upper=z["upper"],
            centers=z["centers"],
            ranges=z["ranges"],
            varnames=[str(v) for v in z["varnames"]],
            obsnames=[str(v) for v in z["obsnames"]],
            latent_case=str(z["latent_case"]),
            latent_param=float(z["latent_param"]),
            n_micro=int(z["n_micro"]),
        )
    d = _parse_rda()
    np.savez(
        path,
        lower=d["lower"],
        upper=d["upper"],
        centers=d["centers"],
        ranges=d["ranges"],
        varnames=d["varnames"],
        obsnames=d["obsnames"],
        latent_case=np.array(d["latent_case"]),
        latent_param=np.array(d["latent_param"]),
        n_micro=np.array(d["n_micro"]),
    )
    return d


if __name__ == "__main__":
    d = load_cars(force=True)
    print("var names :", d["varnames"])
    print("obs names :", d["obsnames"])
    print("latent    :", d["latent_case"], d["latent_param"], "n_micro", d["n_micro"])
    print("lower shape", d["lower"].shape)
    print("lower[:5]\n", np.round(d["lower"][:5], 4))
    print("upper[:5]\n", np.round(d["upper"][:5], 4))
    print("centers[:3]\n", np.round(d["centers"][:3], 4))
    print("ranges[:3]\n", np.round(d["ranges"][:3], 4))
    c = (d["lower"] + d["upper"]) / 2.0
    r = d["upper"] - d["lower"]
    print("max |center - (lo+up)/2| =", np.abs(c - d["centers"]).max())
    print("max |range  - (up-lo)  | =", np.abs(r - d["ranges"]).max())

"""Port of AIDA's interval geometry (R/int_cov.r, R/int_distances.r).

An interval-valued observation is represented by its center c = (a+b)/2 and its
range r = b-a.  For i.i.d. symmetric latent variables (LatentCase
"U_id_symmetric") the symbolic covariance of (c, r) is

    Sigma_B = Cov(c) + delta * Cov(r),      delta = E[U^2] / 4

and the squared Interval-Mahalanobis distance (Definition 3.1 / Eq. (5)) is

    d^2(x, mu_B) = (c - mu_C)' Sigma_B^{-1} (c - mu_C)
                 + delta (r - mu_R)' Sigma_B^{-1} (r - mu_R).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np


def int_mean(z, X):
    """AIDA int_mean_z: weighted mean of the rows of X with weights z."""
    z = np.asarray(z, dtype=float)
    return (z @ X) / z.sum()


def int_cov_z(z, C, R, delta, ddof=0):
    """AIDA int_cov_z for LatentCase 'U_id_symmetric'.

    ddof=0 gives the 1/m covariance used inside the IMCD concentration steps,
    ddof=1 reproduces R's cov() used by int_cov() on the full data.
    """
    z = np.asarray(z, dtype=float)
    m = z.sum()
    den = m - ddof
    mc = (z @ C) / m
    mr = (z @ R) / m
    cc = (C * z[:, None]).T @ C / den - m / den * np.outer(mc, mc)
    rr = (R * z[:, None]).T @ R / den - m / den * np.outer(mr, mr)
    return cc + delta * rr


def safe_inv(S):
    """AIDA safe_solve_cov: ordinary inverse, generalised inverse if singular."""
    try:
        return np.linalg.inv(S)
    except np.linalg.LinAlgError:
        return np.linalg.pinv(S)


def mahal(X, mu, Sinv):
    D = X - mu
    return np.einsum("ij,jk,ik->i", D, Sinv, D)


def imah_dist(C, R, Sinv, mu_c, mu_r, delta):
    """Squared Interval-Mahalanobis distance of every row to the barycenter."""
    return mahal(C, mu_c, Sinv) + delta * mahal(R, mu_r, Sinv)


def classical_fit(C, R, delta):
    """AIDA int_cov / IMah_dist on the full data (non-robust baseline)."""
    S = int_cov_z(np.ones(C.shape[0]), C, R, delta, ddof=1)
    return int_mean(np.ones(C.shape[0]), C), int_mean(np.ones(C.shape[0]), R), S

"""Port of AIDA's farness outlier score (R/farness.r) and of the robust
Yeo-Johnson ML fit it relies on (cellWise::transfo, robust=TRUE).

Steps (Section 3 of the paper):
  1. median / MAD standardise the squared distances,
  2. apply a Yeo-Johnson transformation whose lambda is the ML estimate,
  3. median / MAD standardise the transformed values again,
  4. map to (0, 1) with the normal CDF; scores > 0.9 are flagged.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
from scipy import optimize, stats

MAD_CONST = 1.482602218505602  # R's mad() constant


def mad(x):
    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=float)
    return MAD_CONST * np.median(np.abs(x - np.median(x)))


def yeo_johnson(y, lam):
    y = np.asarray(y, dtype=float).copy()
    low = y < 0
    out = np.empty_like(y)
    if lam != 0:
        out[~low] = ((1.0 + y[~low]) ** lam - 1.0) / lam
    else:
        out[~low] = np.log1p(y[~low])
    if lam != 2:
        out[low] = -((1.0 - y[low]) ** (2.0 - lam) - 1.0) / (2.0 - lam)
    else:
        out[low] = -np.log(1.0 - y[low])
    return out


def _profile_ll(lam, x):
    """cellWise estML(type='YJ') profile log-likelihood (up to a constant)."""
    n = x.size
    xt = yeo_johnson(x, lam)
    mu = xt.mean()
    s2 = np.mean((xt - mu) ** 2)
    return (-0.5 * n * np.log(2 * np.pi)
            - 0.5 * n * np.log(s2)
            - 0.5 / s2 * np.sum((xt - mu) ** 2)
            + (lam - 1.0) * np.sum(np.sign(x) * np.log1p(np.abs(x))))


def ml_yeo_johnson(x, lam_range=(-4.0, 6.0)):
    """ML lambda of the Yeo-Johnson transform, as cellWise::estML does."""
    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=float)
    res = optimize.minimize_scalar(lambda lam: -_profile_ll(lam, x),
                                   bounds=lam_range, method="bounded",
                                   options={"xatol": 1e-6})
    return float(res.x)


def farness(dist, cutoff=None):
    """Return (scores in [0,1], cutoff in squared-distance units or None)."""
    dist = np.asarray(dist, dtype=float)
    nz = dist > 1e-10
    d = dist[nz]

    farloc = np.median(d)
    farsca = mad(d)
    if farsca < 1e-10:
        farsca = np.std(d, ddof=1)
    sfar = (d - farloc) / farsca

    lam = ml_yeo_johnson(sfar)
    xt = yeo_johnson(sfar, lam)

    tfarloc = np.median(xt)
    tfarsca = mad(xt)
    zt = (xt - tfarloc) / tfarsca

    probs = np.zeros_like(dist)
    probs[nz] = stats.norm.cdf(zt)

    cutoff_dist = None
    if cutoff is not None:
        if not 0.0 <= cutoff <= 1.0:
            raise ValueError("cutoff must be in [0, 1]")
        q = stats.norm.ppf(cutoff) * tfarsca + tfarloc   # in Yeo-Johnson space
        new = np.atleast_1d(q)
        low = new < 0
        back = np.empty_like(new)
        if lam != 0:
            back[~low] = (1.0 + lam * new[~low]) ** (1.0 / lam) - 1.0
        else:
            back[~low] = np.exp(new[~low]) - 1.0
        if lam != 2:
            back[low] = 1.0 - (1.0 + (lam - 2.0) * new[low]) ** (1.0 / (2.0 - lam))
        else:
            back[low] = 1.0 - np.exp(-new[low])
        cutoff_dist = float(back[0] * farsca + farloc)
    return probs, cutoff_dist, lam

"""Port of AIDA's reweighted IMCD estimator (R/IMCD.r).

The FAST-MCD idea applied to interval data: draw many small random subsets,
run concentration (C-)steps that keep the h observations with the smallest
squared Interval-Mahalanobis distance, keep the subset with the smallest
determinant of the symbolic covariance matrix, then reweight once with the
farness cutoff.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np

from interval_ops import imah_dist, int_cov_z, int_mean, safe_inv


def _fit(z, C, R, delta):
    S = int_cov_z(z, C, R, delta)
    mu_c = int_mean(z, C)
    mu_r = int_mean(z, R)
    return S, mu_c, mu_r


def _dist(z, C, R, delta):
    S, mu_c, mu_r = _fit(z, C, R, delta)
    return imah_dist(C, R, safe_inv(S), mu_c, mu_r, delta)


def c_step(z, h, C, R, delta):
    d2 = _dist(z, C, R, delta)
    new_z = np.zeros_like(z)
    new_z[np.argsort(d2, kind="stable")[:h]] = 1.0
    S, mu_c, mu_r = _fit(new_z, C, R, delta)
    return new_z, S, mu_c, mu_r


def step_it(z, h, C, R, delta, it=0, max_iter=200):
    """AIDA step_it: it=0 runs C-steps until the determinant stops decreasing."""
    z, S, mu_c, mu_r = c_step(z, h, C, R, delta)
    det_new = np.linalg.det(S)
    if it == 0:
        det_old = np.inf
        reps = 0
        while det_old > det_new and det_new > 0 and reps < max_iter:
            z, S, mu_c, mu_r = c_step(z, h, C, R, delta)
            det_old, det_new = det_new, np.linalg.det(S)
            reps += 1
    else:
        for _ in range(it - 1):
            z, S, mu_c, mu_r = c_step(z, h, C, R, delta)
    return z, S, mu_c, mu_r, det_new


def draw_z(rng, h, C, R, delta):
    """AIDA draw_z: p+1 seed points, extended until the determinant is > 0."""
    n, p = C.shape
    z = np.zeros(n)
    idx = list(rng.choice(n, p + 1, replace=False))
    z[idx] = 1.0
    S = int_cov_z(z, C, R, delta)
    while np.linalg.det(S) == 0 and len(idx) < n - 1:
        cand = [j for j in range(n) if j not in idx]
        j = int(rng.choice(cand))
        idx.append(j)
        z[j] = 1.0
        S = int_cov_z(z, C, R, delta)
    mu_c, mu_r = int_mean(z, C), int_mean(z, R)
    d2 = imah_dist(C, R, safe_inv(S), mu_c, mu_r, delta)
    z = np.zeros(n)
    z[np.argsort(d2, kind="stable")[:h]] = 1.0
    return z


def imcd(C, R, delta, h, seed=20240601, n_starts=500, n_best=10, n_blocks=1):
    """Reweighted-free IMCD: returns the best h-subset found."""
    n = C.shape[0]
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    best = None
    for _ in range(n_blocks):
        zs = [draw_z(rng, h, C, R, delta) for _ in range(n_starts)]
        # 2 C-steps for every start, keep the n_best smallest determinants
        res = [step_it(z, h, C, R, delta, it=2) for z in zs]
        dets = np.array([r[4] for r in res])
        order = np.argsort(dets, kind="stable")[:n_best]
        res = [step_it(res[i][0], h, C, R, delta, it=0) for i in order]
        dets = np.array([r[4] for r in res])
        i = int(np.argmin(dets))
        if best is None or dets[i] < best[4]:
            best = res[i]
    return best  # z, S, mu_c, mu_r, det


def imcd_fit(C, R, delta, h, cutoff=0.9, seed=20240601, n_starts=500,
             n_blocks=1, n_best=10):
    """Full AIDA IMCD(): unweighted IMCD + one farness reweighting step.

    Returns the reweighted barycenter / symbolic covariance, the reweighted
    squared distances and the inlier weights (as int_outliers flags them).
    """
    from farness import farness

    z, S, mu_c, mu_r, det = imcd(C, R, delta, h, seed=seed,
                                 n_starts=n_starts, n_best=n_best,
                                 n_blocks=n_blocks)
    d2 = imah_dist(C, R, safe_inv(S), mu_c, mu_r, delta)
    probs, cut_dist, lam = farness(d2, cutoff)
    w = (probs <= cutoff).astype(float)

    rw_c, rw_r = int_mean(w, C), int_mean(w, R)
    rw_S = int_cov_z(w, C, R, delta)
    rw_d2 = imah_dist(C, R, safe_inv(rw_S), rw_c, rw_r, delta)
    return dict(z=z, det=det, d2_initial=d2, farness_initial=probs,
                cutoff_dist_initial=cut_dist, yj_lambda=lam, w=w,
                mu_c=rw_c, mu_r=rw_r, cov=rw_S, robust_dist=rw_d2)

"""Port of AIDA's closed-form Shapley values (R/Shapley.r) for the
symmetric i.i.d. latent case (delta = E[U^2]/4, Psi = 0).

Theorem 4.1 / Corollary 4.2: the squared Interval-Mahalanobis distance splits
additively into per-variable contributions

    phi_j = c0_j (Sin^-1 c0)_j + delta * r0_j (Sin^-1 r0)_j,

so the cross centers-ranges terms vanish when the latent variables are
symmetric and identically distributed (E[U] = 0 => Psi = 0).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np


def shapley(C, R, mu_c, mu_r, cov, delta):
    Sinv = np.linalg.inv(cov)
    c0 = C - mu_c
    r0 = R - mu_r
    sc = c0 @ Sinv.T           # rows: Sinv c0
    sr = r0 @ Sinv.T           # rows: Sinv r0
    return c0 * sc + delta * r0 * sr


def shapley_decomp(C, R, mu_c, mu_r, cov, delta):
    """Centers / Ranges (and the identically zero cross) contributions."""
    Sinv = np.linalg.inv(cov)
    c0 = C - mu_c
    r0 = R - mu_r
    cen = c0 * (c0 @ Sinv.T)
    rng = delta * r0 * (r0 @ Sinv.T)
    cross = np.zeros_like(cen)  # E[U] = 0 for symmetric latent variables
    return cen, rng, cross


def shapley_interaction(c, r, mu_c, mu_r, cov, delta):
    """Shapley interaction index, Eq. (10)-(12): off-diagonal terms from the
    elementwise product of the outer products with Sinv, diagonal defined so
    that every row sums to the Shapley value of that variable."""
    Sinv = np.linalg.inv(cov)
    c0 = c - mu_c
    r0 = r - mu_r
    inter = 2.0 * np.outer(c0, c0) * Sinv + 2.0 * delta * np.outer(r0, r0) * Sinv
    inter = inter - np.diag(inter.sum(axis=1) / 2.0)
    return inter


def efficiency_error(phi, d2):
    return float(np.max(np.abs(phi.sum(axis=1) - d2)))

"""Reproduce the Cars outlier analysis of
"Explainable Outlier Detection for Interval-valued Data" (arXiv 2606.26307).

Pipeline (ported line-by-line from the AIDA R package, which ships the data):
  intCars (27 car models x 4 interval variables, lnPrice)
    -> reweighted IMCD (h = floor(0.75 n) = 20, farness reweighting at 0.9)
    -> squared robust Interval-Mahalanobis distances
    -> farness outlier scores, flagged when score > 0.9          (Figure 1, C1/C5)
    -> closed-form Shapley values of the six largest distances   (Figure 2a, C3)
    -> centers/ranges decomposition, zero cross terms            (Figure 3a, C6)
    -> Ferrari Shapley interaction tile                          (Figure 3b, R11)

Run `python reproduce.py` for the full result, `--smoke` for a quick check.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import sys
import time

import numpy as np

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(HERE, "src"))

                     shapley_interaction)

CONFIG = dict(
    dataset="Cars (MAINT.Data intCars, AIDA)",
    subset_fraction=0.75,
    farness_cutoff=0.9,
    seed=20240601,
    n_starts_per_block=500,
    n_blocks=4,
    n_best_subsets=10,
    top_k=6,
    interaction_observation="Ferrari",
)

# Reference outlier names quoted in the paper (used only to *score* the run;
# the reported metric value is always recomputed from the data).
PAPER_OUTLIERS = ["MercedesClasseS", "Ferrari", "Porsche", "MercedesSL",
                  "HondaNSK"]


def smoke(cars, delta, h):
    t0 = time.time()
    C, R, labels = cars["centers"], cars["ranges"], cars["obs_names"]
    S = np.linalg.matrix_rank(C)
    fit = imcd_fit(C, R, delta, h, cutoff=CONFIG["farness_cutoff"],
                   seed=CONFIG["seed"], n_starts=50, n_blocks=1)
    d2 = fit["robust_dist"]
    probs, _, _ = farness(d2)
    phi = shapley(C, R, fit["mu_c"], fit["mu_r"], fit["cov"], delta)
    err = efficiency_error(phi, d2)
    out = dict(
        n_obs=int(C.shape[0]), n_vars=int(C.shape[1]),
        center_rank=int(S), det=float(np.linalg.det(fit["cov"])),
        det_positive=bool(np.linalg.det(fit["cov"]) > 0),
        farness_in_unit_interval=bool(np.all((probs >= 0) & (probs <= 1))),
        shapley_efficiency_error=err,
        shapley_efficiency_ok=bool(err < 1e-8),
        first_observation_shapley=[float(v) for v in phi[0]],
        first_observation_distance=float(d2[0]),
        all_finite=bool(np.all(np.isfinite(d2))),
        labels_head=list(labels[:3]),
        runtime_s=round(time.time() - t0, 2),
    )
    out["ok"] = all([out["n_obs"] == 27, out["n_vars"] == 4,
                     out["det_positive"], out["shapley_efficiency_ok"],
                     out["farness_in_unit_interval"], out["all_finite"]])
    return out


def make_plots(cars, fit, probs, d2, top_idx, phi, decomp, inter, outdir):
    import matplotlib
    matplotlib.use("Agg")
    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

    labels = np.asarray(cars["obs_names"])
    flagged = probs > CONFIG["farness_cutoff"]

    # Figure 1: squared robust distances, outliers highlighted, 0.9 cutoff line
    order = np.argsort(-d2)
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 4.2))
    cols = ["dodgerblue" if flagged[i] else "gray50" for i in order]
    ax.bar(np.arange(len(order)), d2[order], color=cols)
    if fit["cutoff_dist_initial"] is not None:

                   label="0.9 farness cutoff")
    ax.set_xticks(np.arange(len(order)))
    ax.set_xticklabels(labels[order], rotation=90, fontsize=7)
    ax.set_ylabel("squared robust Interval-Mahalanobis distance")
    ax.set_title("Cars: reweighted IMCD distances (blue = flagged outlier)")
    ax.legend()

args.summary:
Reproduced the target claim C1 exactly. `python reproduce.py` (no arguments, clean results/) runs in ~9 s end to end and writes results/metrics.json plus four figures.

Approach: the authors' AIDA package is R-only and only python/pip/git are executable here, so I ported the exact Cars pipeline to Python from the shipped R sources and the shipped data (repo/data/intCars.rda, read with the pure-python `rdata` parser; no R, no downloads):
- src/data_io.py: extracts the 27x4 interval Centers/Ranges, car labels, class labels and LatentParam from the S4 object (LowerBounds/UpperBounds derived as Centers -/+ Ranges/2), caches an npz in REPRO_DATA_CACHE.
- src/interval_ops.py: symbolic covariance (int_cov_z, delta = E[U^2]/4 = 1/12) and the squared Interval-Mahalanobis distance (Definition 3.1 / Eq. 5).
- src/imcd.py: faithful port of draw_z / c_step / step_it / pick10 / IMCD plus the farness reweighting step.
- src/farness.py: median/MAD -> ML Yeo-Johnson (cellWise::estML path, not the hubhub-robust variant) -> median/MAD -> normal CDF, with the cutoff mapped back to distance units.
- src/shapley.py: closed-form Shapley values, centers/ranges decomposition (Psi = 0) and the Shapley interaction index with the diagonal rule making row sums equal the Shapley values.

Results (all computed from the data, no paper numbers hard-coded): h = floor(0.75*27) = 20 (74.07%); reweighted IMCD with 2000 random starts (4 blocks, determinant identical across blocks, relative spread 0); 5 observations flagged at farness > 0.9, in descending distance order: MercedesClasseS, Ferrari, Porsche, MercedesSL, HondaNSK — exact label match with the paper's Figure 1 set. Dataset check: 27 observations x 4 interval variables (lnPrice, EngCap, Top Speed, Acceleration). Figure 2a diagnostic: the six largest squared distances are exactly those five plus Bmwserie7. Shapley efficiency error 1.4e-14 (<1e-8); maximum absolute cross centers-ranges contribution exactly 0; Ferrari interaction row sums match the Shapley values to 3.6e-15. Reweighted inlier set 21/27 (77.8%).

Assumptions recorded: h = floor(0.75 n) = 20 (matches the AIDA vignette); farness cutoff 0.9 used both for IMCD reweighting and flagging (AIDA's own reweighting default is 0.95 — noted, medium risk); uniform latent variables delta = 1/12 taken from intCars; numpy RNG with 4 blocks x 500 starts replaces R's sample().
